AC.name: Ascension Island
AC.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.note: Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2021 art. 20: life + 50 from 1 January after death (Arabic PDF could not be machine-read; term consistent across law-firm summaries and the 2002 law it replaced).

AF.name: Afghanistan
AF.note: Law of 2008 (Copyright Law), art. on duration: 50 years after death. Calendar years in the Afghan (solar hijri) calendar, so year-end is the end of the Afghan year, not 31 December.

AG.name: Antigua and Barbuda
AG.note: Copyright Act 2003 s. 10(1): 50 years from end of year of death.

AI.name: Anguilla
AI.note: No primary source reached in the 2026-11-12 research: treated as the strictest until the lawyer checks it.

AO.name: Angola
AO.note: Law 15/14 art. 72: life + 70 from 1 January after death.

AQ.name: Antarctica
AQ.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.note: Law 11.723 art. 5 (as amended by Law 24.870 of 1997): 70 years from 1 January after death. Whether the 1997 extension revived works already free (authors who died before 1947) was not confirmed, so freeIfDiedBefore is left null.

AT.name: Austria
AT.note: Urheberrechtsgesetz § 60: 70 years after death; rule of the shorter term via EU Term Directive art. 7.

AU.name: Australia
AU.note: Copyright Act 1968 s. 33: 70 years after the calendar year of death. Extension took effect 1 January 2005 and did not revive expired copyright, so authors who died before 1955 are free (National Library of Australia). Australia is believed not to apply the rule of the shorter term but no statutory text was checked; null. Works unpublished at death had special rules before 2019.

AW.name: Aruba
AW.note: No primary source reached in the 2026-11-12 research: treated as the strictest until the lawyer checks it.

AZ.name: Azerbaijan
AZ.note: Law of 1996 (as amended) art. 25: life + 70; the extension applies to all works whose term had not expired when it entered into force.

BA.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
BA.note: Law on Copyright and Related Rights 2010 art. 55: life + 70.

BB.name: Barbados
BB.note: Copyright Act Cap. 300 s. 10(1): life + 50 calendar years.

BD.name: Bangladesh
BD.note: Copyright Act 2023 (Bengali text; PDF not machine-readable here). Life + 60 as in the 2000 Act s. 24; confirm in the 2023 Act.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.note: Code of Economic Law art. XI.166 §1: 70 years after death. EU Term Directive art. 7 applies. Belgium had wartime extensions (laws of 1921 and 1947); they are understood to be absorbed by the 1994 life+70 rule, not checked further.

BG.name: Bulgaria
BG.note: Law on Copyright art. 27(1): life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

BH.name: Bahrain
BH.note: Law 22 of 2006 art. 37: life + 70 from 1 January after death.

BI.name: Burundi
BI.note: Law 1/021 of 2005 art. 58: life + 50 calendar years.

BJ.name: Benin
BJ.note: Law 2005-30 art. 52: life + 70 calendar years. (Some secondary lists still say 50.)

BM.name: Bermuda
BM.note: Copyright and Designs Act 2004 s. 21: 50 years from end of year of death (UK 1956 model).

BN.name: Brunei
BN.note: Emergency (Copyright) Order 1999 s. 14(1): 50 years from end of year of death.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.note: Law 9.610/1998 art. 41: 70 years from 1 January after death.

BS.name: Bahamas
BS.note: Copyright Act Ch. 323 s. 10(1) as amended 2004: 70 years from end of year of death; s. 10(7) applies the country-of-origin term if shorter for foreign works. Wikipedia lists only 'Berne', so this is worth a second look.

BW.name: Botswana
BW.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act Cap. 68:02 s. 10(1): life + 50.

BY.name: Belarus
BY.note: Law 262-Z of 2011: life + 50 from 1 January after death. The country-of-origin clause found concerns treaty protection of works not yet public domain there, not a general shorter-term rule.

BZ.name: Belize
BZ.note: Copyright Act Cap. 252 s. 10(1): 50 years from end of year of death.

CA.name: Canada
CA.note: Copyright Act s. 6: life + 70 to the end of the calendar year, in force 30 December 2022. Budget Implementation Act 2022 No. 1 s. 280: the extension does not revive expired copyright, so authors who died before 1972 are free. No comparison-of-terms rule in the Act.

CD.name: DR Congo
CD.note: Ordinance-Law 86-033: 50 years from 1 January after death.

CF.name: Central African Republic
CF.note: Ordinance 85.002 art. 41: 50 years (scanned text; Central African Republic is also an OAPI member, Bangui Agreement Annex VII also life + 50).

CG.name: Republic of the Congo
CG.note: Law 24-82 of 1982 art. 61: life + 50 (old law; OAPI Annex VII also life + 50).

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.note: URG art. 29(2)(b): 70 years after death (computer programs 50). The Act has no comparison-of-terms clause.

CI.name: Côte d'Ivoire
CI.note: Law 2016-555 art. 47: life + 70 calendar years. The repealed Law 96-564 of 1996 gave life + 99; art. 150 applies the new law to existing works, so 70 now applies to all, but a reviewer should confirm that rights vested under the 99-year term were not preserved.

CK.name: Cook Islands
CK.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

CN.name: China
CN.note: Copyright Law art. 23: life + 50, ending 31 December of the 50th year after death.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.note: Law 23 of 1982 art. 21 (still in force after Law 1915 of 2018): life + 80.

CR.name: Costa Rica
CR.note: Law 6683 art. 58 (as amended by Law 8686 of 2008): 70 years after death (Spanish consolidated text in WIPO Lex).

CV.name: Cabo Verde
CV.note: Decree-Law 1/2009 art. 25: 50 years after death; foreign works get no more than the country-of-origin term.

CW.name: Curaçao
CW.note: Auteursverordening 1913 (consolidated 2025) art. 38(1): 50 years counted from the day of the author's death, not from the end of the year.

CY.name: Cyprus
CY.note: Law 59/1976 as amended, s. 5: 70 years from death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.note: Act 121/2000 art. 27(1): life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

DE.name: Germany
DE.note: UrhG § 64: 70 years after death (since 1965); EU Term Directive art. 7.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.note: Consolidated Act 1093/2023 § 63: 70 years after the year of death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

DO.name: Dominican Republic
DO.note: Law 65-00 art. 21 as amended by Law 424-06 (DR-CAFTA): life + 70. The WIPO Lex text is the unamended 2000 law (life + 50); source is the official Law 424-06.

DZ.name: Algeria
DZ.note: Ordinance 03-05 art. 54: 50 years from 1 January after death.

EE.name: Estonia
EE.note: Copyright Act § 38(1): life + 70; § 92 applies the country-of-origin term for third-country works.

EH.name: Western Sahara
EH.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

ER.name: Eritrea
ER.note: Civil Code of 2015 art. 1180: 50 years after 1 January following death; protection cannot be invoked if expired in the country of origin.

ES.name: Spain
ES.note: Ley de Propiedad Intelectual art. 26: life + 70. Disposición transitoria cuarta: authors who died before 7 December 1987 keep the 1879 Law term (life + 80). Foreign works from third countries: country-of-origin term, capped.

FI.name: Finland
FI.note: Copyright Act 404/1961 § 43: 70 years from the year of death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

FJ.name: Fiji
FJ.note: Copyright Act 1999 s. 22(1): 50 years after end of year of death.

FK.name: Falkland Islands
FK.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

FO.name: Faroe Islands
FO.note: No primary source reached in the 2026-11-12 research: treated as the strictest until the lawyer checks it.

FR.name: France

exceptions.note: L123-9: works published before 1 Jan 1948 and not public domain on 13 Aug 1941; musical works only (70 + 8y120d, rounded up)
L123-8 + L123-9: works published before the end of 1920 get both extensions (6y152d + 8y120d); musical works

exceptions.condition: author recorded as "mort pour la France"
exceptions.note: L123-10: +30 years on top of the extended term; 109 assumes a pre-1948 musical work (70 + 8y120d + 30, rounded up); 100 otherwise

FR.note: Code de la propriété intellectuelle L123-1: 70 years after the year of death; L123-12 rule of the shorter term. Wartime extensions (L123-8, L123-9) and 'mort pour la France' (L123-10) still add time for musical works: under the 1985 law music already had 70 years, so the extensions survived the 1997 harmonisation (Ravel's Bolero entered the French public domain only in 2016). See exceptions; the year-end values are rounded up to the next whole year.

GA.name: Gabon
GA.note: Law 1/87 of 1987: life + 50 (scanned text). OAPI Annex VII also life + 50.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.note: CDPA 1988 s. 12(2): 70 years from end of year of death; s. 12(6): non-UK works get their country-of-origin term if shorter. The 1995 regulations revived works for which the term had ended, so no cut-off year.

GE.name: Georgia
GE.note: Law on Copyright and Related Rights: life + 70.

GG.name: Guernsey
GG.note: Copyright (Bailiwick of Guernsey) Ordinance 2005 s. 13(1): 70 years from end of year of death (Guernsey IP Office; consolidated text not opened).

GI.name: Gibraltar
GI.note: Intellectual Property (Copyright and Related Rights) Act 2005 s. 15(2): 70 years from end of year of death; s. 15(6): works whose country of origin is not Gibraltar or the UK get their country-of-origin term if shorter.

GN.name: Guinea
GN.note: Law L/2019/0028/AN art. 39 reads 'soixante-dix (80) ans': the words say 70 and the figure says 80. The longer reading (80) is used; a reviewer should check the official gazette.

GQ.name: Equatorial Guinea
GQ.note: No modern copyright statute found in WIPO Lex. The Spanish Law of 10 January 1879 (life + 80) appears to remain applicable; Equatorial Guinea is also an OAPI member (Bangui Agreement Annex VII, life + 50). The longer reading (80) is used.

GR.name: Greece
GR.note: Law 2121/1993 art. 29: life + 70 from 1 January after death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

GS.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
GS.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

GT.name: Guatemala
GT.note: Law on Copyright (Decree 33-98 as amended) art. 43: life + 75.

GW.name: Guinea-Bissau
GW.note: Only text found is the Portuguese Copyright Code of 1966 (Decree-Law 46.980) extended to Guinea-Bissau: art. 25 life + 50, art. 26 caps foreign works at the country-of-origin term. A newer law may exist (Guinea-Bissau is an OAPI member, Annex VII also life + 50).

GY.name: Guyana
GY.note: UK Copyright Act 1956 as applied in Guyana (Cap. 74): 50 years from end of year of death.

HK.name: Hong Kong
HK.note: Copyright Ordinance Cap. 528 s. 17(2): 50 years from end of year of death. No comparison-of-terms rule was confirmed.

HN.name: Honduras
HN.note: Law on Copyright (Decree 4-99-E as amended by 16-2006) art. 44: life + 75; for foreign authors' works first published abroad the term does not exceed that of the country of origin.

HR.name: Croatia
HR.note: Copyright and Related Rights Act 2021 art. 119: life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

HT.name: Haiti
HT.note: Decree of 12 October 2005 art. 20: life + 60 (scanned PDF hard to read; collective and audiovisual works also 60 years).

HU.name: Hungary
HU.note: Act LXXVI of 1999 art. 31: life + 70 from 1 January after death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.note: Law 28 of 2014 art. 58(1): life + 70 from 1 January after death. Whether the 2014 extension (from 50) revived expired works was not confirmed.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.note: Copyright and Related Rights Act 2000 s. 24(1): 70 years after death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

IL.name: Israel
IL.note: Copyright Act 2007 s. 38: life + 70; s. 44 limits works first published abroad (and some others) to their country-of-origin term; s. 39 ends terms on 31 December.

IM.name: Isle of Man
IM.note: Copyright Act 1991 s. 12(2) as amended: 70 years from end of year of death. The extension from 50 did not revive expired copyright (unlike the UK), but its date was not confirmed, so freeIfDiedBefore is null.

IN.name: India

exceptions.condition: work not published, performed or broadcast before the author died
exceptions.note: Copyright Act s. 24: 60 years from first publication

IN.note: Copyright Act 1957 s. 22: 60 years from the beginning of the year after death. Extended from 50 to 60 by the 1992 amendment (deemed in force 28 December 1991), which did not revive expired works, so authors who died before 1941 are free. International Copyright Order 1999 para. 7: foreign works get no more than their country-of-origin term.

IO.name: British Indian Ocean Territory
IO.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

IR.name: Iran
IR.note: 1970 Act art. 12 (WIPO English text) says 30 years after death; it was amended in 2010 (1389) to 50 years. The amendment text was not found in WIPO Lex; the longer term is used.

IS.name: Iceland
IS.note: Copyright Act 73/1972 art. 43: 70 years from end of year of death; EEA (Term Directive).

IT.name: Italy

exceptions.note: D.Lgs.Lgt. 440/1945: +6 years for works published before it took effect; may be absorbed (uncertain)

IT.note: Law 633/1941 art. 25 (raised to 70 by Law 52/1996 art. 17); EU Term Directive art. 7. A 6-year wartime extension (D.Lgs.Lgt. 440/1945) applied to works published before the war; Italian courts have treated it as absorbed for some categories, but no ruling on music under the 70-year term was found, so it is listed as an exception (stricter reading).

JE.name: Jersey
JE.note: Intellectual Property (Unregistered Rights) (Jersey) Law 2011 art. 25(2): 70 years from end of year of death (consolidated text listed; wording from secondary summaries).

JM.name: Jamaica
JM.note: Copyright Act 1993 as amended by Act 13 of 2015: life + 95 (JIPO). The 2015 extension reached back to works whose 50-year term expired from 1 January 2012, so authors who died in 1962 or later get 95; earlier ones stay free. The WIPO Lex PDF is a poor scan; source is the Jamaica IP Office.

JP.name: Japan

exceptions.condition: work owned by a national of an Allied Power during WWII (from 8 Dec 1941 or later accession, to the peace treaty)
exceptions.note: Act No. 302 of 1952; 3,794 days for US/UK/FR/CA/AU, rounded up; longer for some countries. Because the additions sat on top of the old life+50 term, Allied works of authors who died as late as 1957 were still protected on 30 Dec 2018 and got the extension; 1957 is the stricter cut-off.

JP.note: Copyright Act art. 51: 70 years after death (in force 30 December 2018, not retroactive: authors who died before 1968 are free). Art. 58: rule of the shorter term for Berne/WCT/WTO works. Wartime additions under the 1952 Act on Special Provisions add about 10.4 years (3,794 days for the US, UK, France, Canada, Australia; longer for some others) to works of Allied nationals that existed before or during the war.

KE.name: Kenya
KE.note: Copyright Act Cap. 130 s. 23 table: 50 years after end of year of death.

KG.name: Kyrgyzstan
KG.note: Law of 1998 art. 27: life + 50 from 1 January after death.

KI.name: Kiribati
KI.note: Copyright Act 2018 s. on duration: life + 50 from end of year of death.

KM.name: Comoros
KM.note: Only text in WIPO Lex is the French Law of 11 March 1957 (life + 50). Comoros is an OAPI member: Bangui Agreement Annex VII (2015) art. 26 is also life + 50.

KN.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
KN.note: Copyright Act 2000 s. 10(1): 50 years from end of year of death.

KP.name: North Korea
KP.note: Copyright Law (as amended 2006) art. 23: protected to the 50th year after the author's death. The 2025 Intellectual Property Law does not set a term.

KR.name: South Korea
KR.note: Copyright Act art. 39(1): life + 70 (amended 2011, in force 1 July 2013). Addenda to Act 10807: no protection for works whose rights had expired before entry into force, so authors who died before 1963 are free. A general comparison-of-terms rule for authors' works was not found.

KW.name: Kuwait
KW.note: Law 75 of 2019 art. 23: life + 50 from 1 January after death (Arabic text).

KY.name: Cayman Islands
KY.note: Copyright (Cayman Islands) Order 2015 (UK CDPA 1988 extended): 70 years after death (Cayman Islands IP Office).

KZ.name: Kazakhstan
KZ.note: Law 6-I of 1996 art. 28(1): life + 70; art. 28(9): treaty works get no more than the country-of-origin term.

LA.name: Laos
LA.note: IP Law (2017) art. on copyright term: 50 years after death, to end of calendar year.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.note: Law 75 of 1999 art. 49: life + 50 from end of year of death.

LC.name: Saint Lucia
LC.note: Copyright Act Cap. 13.07 s. 10(1): 50 years from end of year of death.

LI.name: Liechtenstein
LI.note: URG art. 32: 70 years after death; EEA (Term Directive).

LR.name: Liberia
LR.note: Intellectual Property Act 2016 (copyright part): life + 50 after end of year of death.

LT.name: Lithuania
LT.note: Law on Copyright art. 34: life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.note: Law of 18 April 2001 art. 9: 70 years after death; foreign works capped at the Luxembourg and country-of-origin term.

LV.name: Latvia
LV.note: Copyright Law art. 36: life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

LY.name: Libya
LY.note: Law 9 of 1968 art. 20: 25 years after death but never less than 50 years from first publication. A single life+N figure cannot express this; 50 is a safe upper bound (publication precedes death). Libya is not a Berne member.

MA.name: Morocco
MA.note: Law 2-00 as amended (Law 34-05 of 2006) art. 25: life + 70.

MC.name: Monaco
MC.note: Law 491 of 1948 (amended up to 2022) art. 12: life + 50.

MD.name: Moldova
MD.note: Law 230/2022 on Copyright and Neighbouring Rights: life + 70 (PDF could not be read here; same term as the 2010 Law 139).

MH.name: Marshall Islands
MH.note: No general copyright statute found: WIPO Lex lists only the 1991 Unauthorized Copies of Recorded Materials Act, and the Marshall Islands are not in Berne. 50 is a conservative placeholder, not a statutory term.

ML.name: Mali
ML.note: Ordinance 2026-015/PT-RM of 10 April 2026 art. 60: life + 70 from 1 January after death; art. 64: foreign works get the country-of-origin term, capped at Mali's.

MM.name: Myanmar
MM.note: Copyright Law 2019 s. 17: life + 50 after the year of death.

MN.name: Mongolia
MN.note: Law on Copyright and Related Rights 2021 art. 15.3: 50 years after 1 January following death.

MR.name: Mauritania
MR.note: Law on copyright (2018) art. 53: life + 70 from 1 January after death.

MS.name: Montserrat
MS.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

MT.name: Malta
MT.note: Copyright Act Cap. 415 art. 4: 70 years after end of year of death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.note: Federal Copyright Law art. 29(I): life + 100 (since 23 July 2003). Earlier extensions (to 50 in 1982, 75 in 1997, 100 in 2003) are reported not to have revived works already free, which would free authors who died before about 1952, but this was not confirmed from transitional articles; null used.

NA.name: Namibia
NA.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Protection Act 1994: life + 50 from end of year of death.

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.note: Copyright Act 2022 s. 19(1)(a): 70 years after end of year of death (was 70 under the old Act too).

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.note: Auteurswet 1912 art. 37: 70 years from 1 January after death; art. 42: a work whose term has expired in its country of origin cannot be protected in the Netherlands; EU Term Directive art. 7.

NR.name: Nauru
NR.note: Copyright Act 2019 s. 18: life + 50 from end of year of death.

NU.name: Niue
NU.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.note: Copyright Act 1994 s. 22: 50 years from end of year of death. Not yet extended: the NZ-EU and NZ-UK trade agreements require life + 70 by May 2028 and Cabinet agreed the extension in May 2026, but no bill had passed when compiled. Re-check soon.

OM.name: Oman
OM.note: Royal Decree 65/2008 art. 26: life + 70 from 1 January after death.

PE.name: Peru
PE.note: Legislative Decree 822 art. 52: life + 70 'regardless of the country of origin of the work', so no rule of the shorter term.

PG.name: Papua New Guinea
PG.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act 2000 s. 17(1): life + 50.

PK.name: Pakistan
PK.note: Copyright Ordinance 1962 s. 18: 50 years from beginning of year after death.

PL.name: Poland
PL.note: Act of 1994 art. 36: 70 years from death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

PN.name: Pitcairn Islands
PN.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

PR.name: Puerto Rico
PR.note: Puerto Rico is under US federal copyright law (17 U.S.C.): same publication-based rule as the US. Puerto Rico's own Moral Rights Act 2012 does not change the economic term.

PS.name: Palestine
PS.note: No Palestinian copyright statute found; the UK Copyright Act 1911 (as applied by the Copyright Ordinance 1924) is reported to remain in force in the West Bank and Gaza: life + 50. A 2013 draft law was not enacted.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.note: Code of Copyright art. 31: 70 years after death (WIPO's English translation is pre-1997 and still says 50; the consolidated Portuguese text says 70); art. 37 shorter term for foreign works.

PY.name: Paraguay
PY.note: Law 1328/1998 art. 47: life + 70 from 1 January after death.

QA.name: Qatar
QA.note: Law on copyright, art. 15: life + 50 calendar years.

RO.name: Romania
RO.note: Law 8/1996 art. 25(1): life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

RU.name: Russia

exceptions.condition: author worked during or fought in the Great Patriotic War (1941-1945)
author repressed and rehabilitated after death
exceptions.note: term runs from 1 January after the year of rehabilitation

RU.note: Civil Code art. 1281: life + 70 from 1 January after death; +4 years if the author worked during or fought in the Great Patriotic War; for repressed authors rehabilitated after death, 70 years from rehabilitation. Introductory Law 231-FZ art. 6: the 70-year term applies only where the 50-year term had not expired by 1 January 1993 (authors who died before 1943, or before 1939 for war participants, are free). Art. 1256(4): treaty works get no more than the country-of-origin term.

SB.name: Solomon Islands
SB.note: Copyright Act Cap. 138 (UK 1956 model): 50 years from end of year of death.

SD.name: Sudan
SD.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act 2013 s. 10(1)(b): life + 50.

SE.name: Sweden
SE.note: Copyright Act (1960:729) § 43: 70 years after the year of death; EU Term Directive art. 7.

SG.name: Singapore
SG.note: Copyright Act 2021: 70 years after end of year of death. The extension took effect 1 July 2004 and s. 530 does not revive copyright that expired before then, so authors who died before 1954 are free.

SH.name: Saint Helena
SH.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.note: ZASP art. 59: life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

SK.name: Slovakia
SK.note: Copyright Act 185/2015 § 32(1): life + 70; EU Term Directive art. 7.

SL.name: Sierra Leone
SL.note: Copyright Act 2011 s. 21: life + 50 (WIPO PDF is an unreadable scan; term from the Act as summarised by several sources; the Wikipedia list's 'life + 50' agrees). Confirm against the gazette.

SM.name: San Marino
SM.note: Law 8 of 1991 art. 36: life + 50 from end of year of death.

SO.name: Somalia
SO.note: No copyright statute found in WIPO Lex; Somalia is not a Berne member. Life + 50 is a placeholder from older secondary sources; low confidence.

SR.name: Suriname
SR.note: Auteurswet 1913 (as amended to 2015) art. 38: 50 years from 1 January after the year of death.

SS.name: South Sudan
SS.note: No South Sudanese copyright statute found; the Sudanese Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Protection Act 1996 (life + 50) is reported to continue in force. Low confidence.

ST.name: Sao Tome and Principe
ST.note: Copyright Code (Decree-Law 02/2017) art. 31: 70 years after death; art. 37: foreign works get the country-of-origin term if not longer.

SV.name: El Salvador
SV.note: Intellectual Property Law art. 90(a): life + 70 from death.

SX.name: Sint Maarten
SX.note: No primary source reached in the 2026-11-12 research: treated as the strictest until the lawyer checks it.

SY.name: Syria
SY.note: Law on copyright (2013), art. 19: life + 50 after end of year of death.

SZ.name: Eswatini
SZ.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act 2018: life + 50 from end of year of death.

TA.name: Tristan da Cunha
TA.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

TC.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
TC.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

TD.name: Chad
TD.note: Law 005/PR/2003 art. 39: life + 70 calendar years. (Some secondary lists give only 'Berne'.)

TG.name: Togo
TG.note: Copyright law, art. 36: life + 50 calendar years.

TJ.name: Tajikistan
TJ.note: Law on Copyright and Related Rights: life + 50; art. 4: term may not exceed that of the country of origin.

TK.name: Tokelau
TK.note: A territory whose own law the 2026-11-12 research didn't reach: the strictest rule until the lawyer checks it.

TL.name: Timor-Leste
TL.note: Copyright Code (Law 14/2022) arts. 118-119: 50 years after death, counted from 1 January after.

TN.name: Tunisia
TN.note: Law 94-36 (as amended): life + 50 from 1 January after death.

TR.name: Türkiye
TR.note: Law 5846 art. 27: life + 70 (since Law 4110 of 1995). WIPO's PDF could not be machine-read here.

TV.name: Tuvalu
TV.note: Copyright Act Cap. 40.24: life + 50 (PDF not machine-read here).

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.note: Copyright Act art. 30: life + 50; art. 35: terms end on the last day of the last year. Art. 106-1 excludes foreign works already expired in their country of origin only for works restored on WTO accession, not a general shorter-term rule.

TZ.name: Tanzania
TZ.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act Cap. 218 s. 16(1): life + 50. (Zanzibar has its own Copyright Act 2003, not checked.)

UG.name: Uganda
UG.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act Cap. 222 s. 12(1): life + 50.

US.name: United States
US.note: Publication-based for most music and lyrics: works published before 1931 are public domain in 2026; works published 1931-1977 are protected 95 years from publication (to 31 December), regardless of the author's death. 'life' (70) applies to works created since 1978 or never published (17 U.S.C. 302); works published 1931-1977 use publicationBased. No rule of the shorter term.

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.note: Law 9.739 art. 14 as amended by Law 19.857 of 23 December 2019 art. 1: life + 70 (was 50). WIPO's English text predates 2019 and still says 50. Whether the 2019 extension revived works already free was not confirmed; null used.

UZ.name: Uzbekistan
UZ.note: Law 42 of 2006 as amended in 2021, art. 35: life + 70 (was 50). Non-revival not confirmed.

VA.name: Holy See (Vatican City)
VA.note: Law CXCVII of 2017 on copyright: follows Italian Law 633/1941 terms (life + 70); only part of the text was machine-read.

VC.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
VC.note: Copyright Act s. 10(1): 75 years from end of year of death.

VE.name: Venezuela
VE.note: Law on Copyright 1993 art. 25: 60 years from 1 January after death.

VG.name: British Virgin Islands
VG.note: Virgin Islands Copyright Act (UK Copyright Act 1956 as extended, revised edition 2020) s. 2(3): 50 years from end of year of death. (The Wikipedia list's 'life + 70' is not supported by the official text.)

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.note: IP Law art. 27(2)(b): life + 50, ending 31 December.

VU.name: Vanuatu
VU.note: Copyright and Related Rights Act 2000 s. 19 table: life + 50.

XK.name: Kosovo
XK.note: Law 08/L-205 on Copyright and Related Rights (2023), replacing Law 04/L-065 (2011): life + 70 from 1 January after death. Source is the official text of the 2011 law (same term); the 2023 text was not opened.

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.note: Copyright Act 98 of 1978 s. 3(2)(a): life + 50 from end of year of death.

ZM.name: Zambia
ZM.note: Copyright and Performance Rights Act 1994 s. 12(1): 50 years from end of year of death.

ZW.name: Zimbabwe
ZW.note: Copyright and Neighbouring Rights Act Cap. 26:05: life + 50 from end of year of death.

_meta.method: Draft for legal review. For each jurisdiction the current copyright statute was located in WIPO Lex (country profile, 'Main IP Laws'), its text (inline HTML or official PDF) was searched for the general term for works of known authors (musical works and lyrics fall under the general literary/musical rule everywhere checked), and for any comparison-of-terms clause. Where WIPO Lex lacked the text or was out of date, the national gazette, legislature or IP office was used; Wikipedia's list was used only as a lead. Terms were checked against the anchors supplied. Where readings conflicted, the longer term was chosen and the doubt is in 'note'. 'freeIfDiedBefore' is only set where a non-retroactive extension was confirmed; otherwise null (the stricter reading). 'shorterTerm' is true only where a statute applying the rule of the shorter term to foreign works was found; false where the absence is well established; null otherwise. Every term runs to 31 December of the last year unless fromDeathYearEnd is false.
_meta.notIncluded: Aruba, Sint Maarten, Anguilla and the Faroe Islands were left out: no primary source was reached (secondary sources say life + 50, + 50, + 50 and + 70).
_meta.fieldsAdded: exceptions may carry publishedBefore, condition, addYears, addDays, termFromPublication, freeIfDiedBefore and source; some entries carry sourceFreeIfDiedBefore.
